summary: Review/fold/assay the AX spec + slides + constellation for what must be PROTOTYPED (high-risk novel approaches needing a PoC) + HARDENED (soft/un-ratified spec areas) before driving (batched, read-only → backlog)

assay.slice: proto:dock-morph (AX.W01 single-scalar dock morph + AX.W42 unified useLiquidMorph substrate)

prototypeNeeds.item: Single-scalar --dock-morph-t calc-ramp across the D-tier/C-tier axes in one paint (the W01 headline architecture)
prototypeNeeds.risk: W01's central thesis — one normalized 0->1 spring scalar written to --dock-morph-t, with EVERY axis (inline-size, padding, border-radius, scale, bg/border color, child stagger) a pure calc() read off it — is a DIFFERENT morph architecture than what ships. At HEAD useLayerTransition drives the spring in PIXEL space via FLIP (setDim(el, `${w}px`) per frame, the literal measured width), not a 0->1 scalar. The size axis intrinsically needs the JS-measured to-size (you cannot calc() an intrinsic max-content width from a 0->1 t without a measured endpoint), so --dock-morph-t must be DERIVED from the pixel spring ((w - fromSize)/span) and then the OTHER axes calc() off that derived scalar. Whether padding/radius/color tracking the derived scalar reads as 'one continuous spring' co-temporally with the FLIP-driven width — vs subtly leading/lagging because width is pixel-exact and the rest is scalar-interpolated — is exactly the box-vs-content desync class W01 is trying to KILL, re-expressed one layer in. --dock-morph-t does not exist at HEAD (only --dock-morph-progress for stagger, FLIP-only), so this is net-new architecture, not a refactor of an existing scalar.
prototypeNeeds.poc: Spike a single GlassDock with the morph re-expressed as: pixel-space SpringProgress on inline-size (kept) -> write derived t=(w-from)/span to --dock-morph-t on the .glass-dock root each frame -> padding/border-radius/scale all calc() off t in dock.css. Drive a collapse->expand and a mid-flight re-toggle; capture computed padding-inline + border-radius + bounding-width + a child opacity on ONE rAF timeline. Confirm all axes onset same-frame (lead/lag <=1 frame) AND read as one spring. Verify under PRM the scalar snaps. ~1 day; reuses the existing SpringProgress + the dock demo route.

prototypeNeeds.item: @property-registered <number> --morph-t 'composites the morph' perf claim on the layout-tier axes
prototypeNeeds.risk: W01 SOTA fold 1 + W42 fold 1 both assert --morph-t MUST be @property-registered {syntax:'<number>'} so it 'interpolates composited' rather than discretely. This is HALF-true and the load-bearing perf justification: a registered <number> interpolates smoothly on the compositor for the VAR itself, but every axis that calc()s off it (width/padding/border-radius/background) still triggers layout+paint per frame on the MAIN thread — they are not composited. W01 fold 4 itself flags this as 'the EXPENSIVE corner of the 16.67ms budget' and rests the whole thing on 'acceptable ONLY because the clip-reveal aperture makes it paint-bounded not reflow-per-frame'. That paint-bound vs reflow-per-frame claim for a morphing dock with N children laid out once is unproven on a real device, and is the difference between a smooth morph and jank. If it reflows per frame the architecture must move axes to S-tier transform/clip-path (fold 4's own escape hatch) — a materially different impl.
prototypeNeeds.poc: On the W01 spike, attach a Performance-panel / PerformanceObserver longtask + layout-thrash probe (or Chrome trace) across a collapse->expand at 3 viewports and a 20+ child dock; confirm no per-frame forced reflow and frame budget under 16.67ms on the DEFAULT engine. If it thrashes, prototype the transform/clip-path variant for the cheap axes. ~0.5 day on top of the first spike.

prototypeNeeds.item: Velocity-continuous interruptible retarget surviving the 479->~130 re-derivation
prototypeNeeds.risk: The AV.W9.2 velocity-continuity retarget (re-seat the live SpringProgress from (value, velocity) on a mid-flight re-toggle instead of dispose+reconstruct-from-rest) is named the ONE load-bearing iOS-feel piece W01 must preserve through a 73% line-count reduction. At HEAD it is intricate closure machinery: a `live` guard (spring!==null && springEl===el && !settled), fromSize=live.value, re-pin, transitionId guarding stale rAF callbacks, and span re-read so the stagger carries through the interrupt. Collapsing 479->130 while KEEPING this exact behavior is the highest-regression-risk edit in the band — a subtle reordering re-seats from rest and the morph 'snaps' (the non-iOS re-toggle the charter explicitly flags), and the gate's lead/lag assertion would NOT catch a velocity discontinuity (it samples onset co-temporality, not inertia continuity).
prototypeNeeds.poc: Before the rewrite, capture a reference velocity-trace of HEAD's retarget (subscribe to the spring, log value+velocity across an interrupt). After the 130-line rewrite, re-capture and assert no velocity zero-crossing at the re-toggle instant (continuity). Build this trace into the gate-author's adversarial probe — it is the one axis the lead/lag gate misses. ~0.5 day; pure instrumentation, no new infra.

prototypeNeeds.item: useLiquidMorph reuse-ledger reconciliation — useSpring (Vue numeric tracker) vs the dock's raw SpringProgress.play() pixel-space FLIP
prototypeNeeds.risk: W42's ~70%-assembly thesis names `useSpring` as the spring core the substrate reuses ('the keyframes.js LIGHT-barrel core via the existing useSpring'). But the dock does NOT use useSpring — useLayerTransition constructs SpringProgress directly and drives it in PIXEL space via .play((w)=>setDim(el,`${w}px`)), reading .value as the live width. useSpring is a generic Vue-reactive numeric-target tracker (target ref in, value ref out, subscribe-mirror) with no FLIP measurement, no pixel-space size ownership, no clip-aperture lifecycle, no transitionId staleness guard. So the substrate cannot just 'wrap useSpring' for the dock case; the FLIP+measure+retarget+clip-aperture lifecycle (the genuinely-hard 70%) lives in useLayerTransition, not useSpring. The reuse-ledger conflates two different spring surfaces. If useLiquidMorph is built on useSpring it loses the FLIP machinery; if built on raw SpringProgress it duplicates/replaces useSpring. This is an un-ratified API-foundation collision that determines whether the substrate is genuinely ~70% assembly or closer to a re-author.
prototypeNeeds.poc: Census spike: write the useLiquidMorph(elRef, {axes, state}) signature against BOTH the dock (FLIP-measured size) and the proposed 2nd consumer (tab-indicator/card-detail), and trace which existing primitive each line reuses. Confirm whether the size-axis FLIP+measure lifts cleanly out of useLayerTransition into the substrate and whether useSpring is the scalar driver or is bypassed for raw SpringProgress. Output the real net-new vs assembly split. ~1 day; design+trace, no impl.

prototypeNeeds.item: W42 generalization to a genuine 2nd consumer (the ratify-before-impl glass primitive)
prototypeNeeds.risk: The substrate-with-consumer bar (>=2 consumers at landing, fail-closed) hinges on a 2nd consumer that is UNCHOSEN (open question 2: tab-indicator glide / card->detail / dialog materialize / segmented-toggle thumb). The risk: the dock's morph is a FLIP-measured intrinsic-size reshape; most candidate primitives are NOT — a tab-indicator glide is a transform/inset translate (no intrinsic measure), a dialog materialize is @starting-style-native (W42 itself warns this would be a CSS-only-tier consumer that weakens the proof), a card->detail is a layout reshape closer to the dock. If the 2nd consumer's morph shape is too unlike the dock's, the substrate's axes-declaration + size-FLIP API is overfit to the dock and the 2nd consumer only exercises the trivial CSS-calc tier — failing the 'must read BETTER on the substrate, not just compile' close criterion. The generalization is genuinely unproven until a real 2nd consumer is built on the SAME API and reads better, not just passes.

assay.notes:
SLICE VERDICT: W01 and W42 are the two highest-architecture-risk waves in my slice; both rest on a single load-bearing technical assumption that is only PARTLY proven — that a registered --morph-t <number> scalar + CSS calc() across every axis reads as one composited spring. The truth (W01's own SOTA fold 4 admits it): the registered var interpolates smoothly, but the layout/paint-tier axes that calc() off it (width/padding/border-radius/background) still cost main-thread layout+paint per frame; the whole thing is paint-bounded ONLY because the clip-reveal aperture lays content out once. That is the single most important thing to PoC before driving (prototypeNeeds #1 + #2).

SOURCE-GROUNDED COLLISION the specs UNDERSTATE: the dock does NOT drive a 0->1 scalar today — useLayerTransition.ts drives SpringProgress in PIXEL space via FLIP (setDim(el, `${w}px`) per frame), and --dock-morph-t does not exist at HEAD (only --dock-morph-progress for stagger, written FLIP-only). So W01 is net-new morph architecture (derive a 0->1 scalar from the pixel spring, then calc() the rest off it), not a refactor. And W42's reuse-ledger names `useSpring` as the spring core, but useSpring is a generic Vue numeric-target tracker with NO FLIP/pixel-space/clip-aperture machinery — the genuinely-hard 70% lives in useLayerTransition, not useSpring. This conflation (prototypeNeeds #4) determines whether W42 is really ~70% assembly or closer to a re-author.

GENUINE DE-RISK ALREADY DONE (not flagged as risk): W00 pre-solves the gate-feasibility (the keyframes 181-sample no-morph trap) with a deterministic-drive design — forced-FLIP arm + lowered collapse-delay + real page.hover + a --spring-dock token-peak secondary + an optional __springProgress test-seam. That is real, charter-level de-risking; the residual risk is sequencing (W00 must close first; hardeningNeeds #1/#2) not novelty.

WHAT IS NOT FLAGGED (routine, deliberately excluded): the createOptionalContext factory already exists and is canon (dockContext/dockLayerContext use it), so W02's dockMorphContext + W42's MorphGroup DI is assembly not invention; the /dock barrel re-export of useLayerTransition is a one-line add; the value.js fork-deletion is W34 cross-repo (read-only routing, not my slice's build). The fourier route-morph view-transition-name preservation IS flagged (prototypeNeeds #6) because it is a live-behavior separability decision (RATIFY-BEFORE-IMPL) that vue-tsc+units cannot see — only the two-dock co-mount e2e catches a dropped/relocated name.

TWO UN-RATIFIED BLOCKERS gating W42 driving: (1) the 2nd consumer is UNCHOSEN and most candidates exercise only the trivial CSS-calc tier, not the dock's hard size-FLIP machinery — the substrate-with-consumer bar is unenforceable until a real 2nd consumer reads BETTER on the substrate (prototypeNeeds #5). (2) W42-distinct-vs-folded + W42<->W02 ordering are both unratified and both double-touch the band's highest-risk file useLayerTransition.ts (hardeningNeeds #8/#9). Recommend ratifying both at W42 wave-open before any impl.

FILE EVIDENCE: useLayerTransition.ts (479 lines, pixel-space FLIP confirmed at :409 setDim/:325 fromSize=live.value/:319-320 retarget guard); dock.css 1227 lines (morph drivers :326-340 confirmed as CSS-transition on --dock-motion-resize/-standard; stagger calc-ramp :758-795 confirmed FLIP-only via [data-revealing]); GlassDock.vue:191 dockId mint + :280 view-transition-name on .dock-layers; useSpring.ts confirmed a generic Vue numeric tracker (target ref in, subscribe-mirror out, no FLIP); scripts/proof-dock-animation-live.mjs 642 lines confirmed fail-OPEN (exit(0) :559) + samples only .dock-layers width (:145-148), never the root box.

assay.slice: proto:lensing — the lensing-via-feDisplacementMap glass refraction (AX.W20 retire-target + AX.W42 `--glass-refract-scale` spring-off-`--morph-t` fold). prototypeNeeds.item: De-risk the --glass-refract-scale spring-off---morph-t mechanism: prove only `scale` animates without a map rebuild, and that a mid-morph box reshape does NOT regenerate the displacement map. W42 fold 5 (line 148-154) and synthesis:71 both assert 'only scale animates cheaply; a shape/size change forces a full displacement-map rebuild, so NEVER regenerate the map mid-morph.' --glass-refract-scale is NOT registered as a @property at HEAD (grep confirms zero in src/styles). The feDisplacementMap `scale` attribute is NOT a CSS custom property — it is an SVG attribute baked into the data-URI filter string, so a CSS var() cannot reach it without re-emitting the whole url(). This is an unvalidated assumption: there may be NO cheap CSS path to animate the displacement scale at all without rebuilding the data-URI.

prototypeNeeds.risk: W13 requires van-Gogh to read as 'sparse, high-contrast, with visible inter-stroke canvas gaps ... each stroke reads as a separable mark, not a coverage smear.' But the existing engine (`bestOil` + `paintOver`, aurora.frag.ts:406 `col = mediumVangogh(col,...)`) is a FULL-COVERAGE field by construction: `bestOil` returns the best-of-9 covering stroke for EVERY pixel and `paintOver` always composites onto the running color. There is no 'bare canvas' concept — un-covered pixels still show the warped aurora base, not a Van-Gogh ground.
